subject: tech
title: Kind and Safe Online
about: Being kind and staying safe online: kind words and the would-I-say-it-to-their-face test, what to do when someone is unkind or a stranger messages, prize pop-ups, stopping and telling when something feels yucky, taking turns and sharing in games, giving credit for a friend's drawing or idea, asking before sharing a photo, screen-time balance and pause-and-think. NC K2-IC-03 (work respectfully and responsibly with others online), K2-AP-06 (give attribution) and K2-NI-03 (your digital footprint). Read it together: the tablet reads every question and choice aloud.
tip: Before he taps anything new, say the two words with him: pause and think.

cards.q: Before you type a message to a friend, what kind of words do you use?
cards.note: Typed words can hurt too. Use words that would make your friend smile.

cards.q: Here is a test for a message: would you say it to the person's face? If no, what do you do?
cards.note: If you would not say it face to face, it does not belong in a message either.

cards.q: Someone online says something mean to you. What do you do first?
cards.note: You do not have to answer mean words. A grown-up can help, and it is never your fault.

cards.q: You see a kid being mean to your friend in a game. What can you do?
cards.note: Do not type back at the mean kid. A grown-up can stop it, and your friend will feel better.

cards.q: A message pops up from someone you do not know. What do you do?
cards.note: You do not have to answer anyone you do not know. Your grown-up decides if it is safe.

cards.q: A pop-up says, you won a prize! Tap here! Should you tap it?
cards.note: Pop-ups that promise prizes are tricks. Show a grown-up and they will close it.

cards.q: Something on the screen makes you feel yucky or scared. What is the smart move?
cards.note: Turn the screen over and get a grown-up. You are never in trouble for telling.

cards.q: You and a friend both want to play the same tablet game. What is a fair way?
cards.note: Taking turns online works just like at the playground. A timer helps.

cards.q: Two of you are building in a game together. How do you work well as a team?
cards.note: Teams online share the work and listen to each other's ideas.

cards.q: You use your friend's drawing in your project. What do you say?
cards.note: Giving credit means saying who made it. It is honest and makes your friend proud.

cards.q: You build a tower from a plan you saw in a video. What do you tell people?
cards.note: Programmers give credit too. When you use someone's idea, say where it came from.

cards.q: You took a funny photo of your friend. What do you do before you share it?
cards.note: A photo belongs to the person in it. Ask your friend, and ask a grown-up, before it goes anywhere.

cards.q: You have played on the tablet for a while. What is a good thing to do next?
cards.note: Screens are fun, but bodies need running, jumping and fresh air too. That is balance.

cards.q: Before you tap a new button or link, what two words do you remember?
cards.note: Pause and think: is this safe? Is this kind? If you are not sure, ask.

cards.q: Your friend types, my tower fell down, I am sad. What is a kind thing to type back?
cards.note: Kind words help a friend feel better online too.

cards.q: Who makes the rules about which games and videos are okay for you?
cards.note: Grown-ups pick what is right for your age. If you are not sure, ask.
